prepared_by: project development with Codex; developer-visible, not blind

upstream.license_review: LICENSE expressly covers all repository parts except enumerated dataset components. text_attack_train.json is attack data per benchmark/README.md and is not one of the enumerated third-party exceptions. MIT attribution retained. No external context datasets imported.
upstream.collection: GitHub connector read-only fetch of pinned commit, LICENSE, benchmark README and the small attack JSON. No upstream dependencies, agent environment or model requests.

limitations: Small purposeful diagnostic corpus, not representative of real-world frequency.
All holdout examples were visible during corpus construction; no blind independent evaluation claim.
Four source attack payloads adapted into email/document wrappers and Russian paraphrases; these are not original upstream EmailQA examples.
Upstream attack success and labels were not imported; attack indicates instruction-injection intent in the constructed external context.
No LLMail-Inject rows or AgentDojo scenarios imported; one verified source suffices for Phase 6.
split_revision_note: v2.2 corrects semantic grouping from the initial developer-visible v2.1 draft. Shared BIPIA wrappers move together to holdout. Educational quotations, privileged extraction, authority spoofing and control-bypass variants each stay in dev. IDs, inputs, labels, expected actions and source/content hashes are unchanged; ID prefixes do not encode current split.
